title: Workload Identity Federation: authenticating from outside without a key

videos.script: A program outside Google Cloud usually already has a signed statement of who it is. A GitHub job can get one that says which repository it runs in. {{statement}} Workload Identity Federation is Google agreeing to trust that statement, on conditions you write. {{trust}} The job sends its token to Google's token service. The service checks the signature, reads the claims, and applies your condition. {{sts}} If the condition passes, the job gets a Google token for an hour. Often it trades that once more, for a service account's token. {{trade}} No key is created anywhere. Nothing long-lived ever crosses. {{nokey}} The condition is the lock on the door. GitHub signs tokens for millions of repositories, with the same issuer. Without a condition, any of them would do. {{lock}} You will plan a pool for the planner's CI, with two locks. Then gcloud writes the credential file a workflow uses. It holds no secret. {{file}} And you send Google the exchange itself, and read why it refuses. {{end}}
